THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

Split Plate Buffalo Wing Night

Frozen wings + protein blue cheese crema = junk dinner becomes high-protein comfort food. The crema does the leverage work — adds protein, satiation, mouthfeel, and turns 'okay frozen wings' into 'restaurant Friday night'.

YIELD4 servings
TOTAL TIME25 min
COOK METHODAir fryer
EST. / SERVING~540 cal | ~44g protein
KEY TO SUCCESS: Air fry from frozen at 400°F for 18-22 min, shake basket halfway. Don't crowd — single layer, space between wings, or they steam instead of crisp.

Ingredients

WINGS

  • 1 bag Kinder's Buttery Buffalo Party Wings (19 oz frozen, includes buffalo sauce packet)

KID CARB

  • 1 box Rudi's Three Cheese Texas Toast (4 thick slices — kid gets 1)

ADULT FINISH

  • Included Kinder's buffalo sauce packet (full)
  • 2 tbsp fresh chives or scallions, chopped (the visual fix)
  • 1 ramekin Protein Blue Cheese Crema (dip)
  • Baby carrots

VEG

  • 1 lb baby carrots (or carrot sticks)

SAUCE (mandatory)

  • 1 batch Protein Blue Cheese Crema (~8 servings, made ahead — gets better on day 2)

Option 1

  • 1 slice Rudi's Three Cheese Texas Toast (toasted)
  • Baby carrots
  • 1 small ramekin Protein Blue Cheese Crema (OPTIONAL — as a dip, not a topping)

Option 2

  • 1 slice Rudi's Three Cheese Texas Toast (toasted)
  • Baby carrots
  • 1 small ramekin Protein Blue Cheese Crema (OPTIONAL — as a dip, not a topping)

Allergens: dairy, gluten.

AT THE TONGS. Same wings, same air-fryer batch. After the 1-min rest: pull kid portion (4-5 wings) into their tray FIRST, then toss the rest aggressively in the included Kinder's buffalo sauce.

Method

Shared base

  1. 1.MAKE THE CREMA AHEAD. 5 min prep + 10 min rest. Cottage cheese + 365 blue cheese + Fairlife + lemon + SPG → blend smooth → fold in chives + chunks. Fridge until serving. (See Protein Blue Cheese Crema in Cookbook.)
  2. 2.AIR FRY WINGS. From frozen, 400°F for 18-22 min. Single layer, shake basket halfway. Crispy = goal. Soggy = overcrowded.
  3. 3.TOAST THE BREAD. Last 6-7 min of the wing cook, slide Rudi's Three Cheese Texas Toast into a toaster oven or air fryer at 400°F. Pull when cheese is melted and edges are golden.
  4. 4.REST. Wings to a clean bowl. 1 minute. DO NOT skip — this is the move that prevents soggy sauced wings.

Adult — Sauced Wings + Crema Dip + Chives

  1. 5.PULL KID WINGS FIRST. Move 4-5 wings to kid tray BEFORE saucing. No going back once they're sauced.
  2. 6.TOSS AGGRESSIVELY. Adult wings in a bowl. Pour the included Kinder's buffalo sauce over. Tongs, toss HARD until every wing is glossy. This is not a delicate move.
  3. 7.PLATE. Sauced wings on a round plate. Square ramekin of Protein Blue Cheese Crema beside. Pile of baby carrots. Chives scattered over the wings — the green is the fix.

Kid — Naked Wings + Crema Dip + Texas Toast · Option 1

  1. 5.PLATE. Divided tray. Unsauced wings in main section, carrots + crema dip ramekin in the side compartment, toasted Rudi's Three Cheese in the bottom compartment. Don't pre-dip. Don't pre-sauce. Don't pre-fold. They commit at their own pace.

Kid — Naked Wings + Crema Dip + Texas Toast · Option 2

  1. 5.Cook 4-5 plain frozen wings in the same air fryer (separate basket or stagger). Brush with butter + tiny pinch of salt. Serve same way as Standard.

SPLIT PLATE SERVING

Adult — Sauced Wings + Crema Dip + Chives: Serve the adult portion as described above.

Kid — Naked Wings + Crema Dip + Texas Toast: Serve the kid portion as described above.

Keys to success

  • REST 1 minute after pulling. This is non-negotiable. Tossing in sauce immediately = sauce absorbs into hot wings and dulls. Rest then toss.
  • TOSS AGGRESSIVELY: Adult wings into a large bowl, pour ALL the included buffalo sauce, toss with tongs hard until every wing is glossy. If you're being gentle, you're doing it wrong.

If something fails

Wings are soggy / not crispy: Overcrowded the air fryer basket. Single layer, space between. Shake halfway. If using a Cosori-style multi-rack, swap racks at the halfway mark too.

Sauce coverage is uneven (some glossy, some dry): You didn't rest the wings before tossing, OR you tossed gently. Rest 1 min full stop, then toss with tongs hard in a bowl until every wing is glossy. This is the move.

Wings taste flat after saucing: Sauce was added to wings that were too hot — it absorbed. Always rest first.

Kid won't eat the wings even unsauced: Kinder's are pre-seasoned (mild spice in the seasoning even before saucing). If kid is super spice-sensitive, use plain frozen wings + butter brush for kids — same crispy texture, zero seasoning.

Plate looks flat in photos / on the table: All orange. Add chives or scallions on adult plate, and the white crema dip on the side. Green + white + orange = balanced visual.

Kid won't dip: Don't push. The dip is OPTIONAL on the kid plate. They might just eat the wing and bread. That's a win. Sauce-as-dip means optional, not required.

Storage and reheating

Store: Wings: best fresh out of the air fryer. Leftover sauced wings keep 2 days in fridge. Crema: 5-7 days.

Reheat: Wings: air fryer 375°F for 3-4 min to re-crisp (microwave = soggy). Crema: serve cold.

Lasts: Wings 2 days. Crema 5-7 days (gets better).

Brands I use

Kinder's
Buttery Buffalo Party Wings (19 oz frozen)
Pre-cooked, pre-seasoned wings with the buffalo sauce packet included. Anaheim chilis + red jalapeño + garlic in the sauce = real buffalo flavor, not gas-station mild. The leverage move: frozen wings that don't taste frozen.
Rudi's Bakery
Three Cheese with Garlic Texas Toast
Real cheese, real bread (Rocky Mountain Sourdough), real butter — not soy or palm oil. The kid carb that earns its slot. 4 thick slices per box.
Protein Blue Cheese Crema
Mandatory cross-link
The sauce IS the meal's leverage. Without it, frozen wings are 'okay'. With it, the meal is high-protein comfort food. Made ahead (8 servings, 5 days fridge life).
